Why go: three southern islands on your own boat

Most Pig Island trips visit two islands. This private longtail day adds a third, Koh Rap, and makes the whole trip yours: a traditional longtail and captain for 5–6 hours, for up to 8 guests, at 8,450 THB per boat. That is about 1,060 THB each for a group of eight. You leave from Thong Krut, the fishing village on Samui's south-west tip, and each crossing between the islands is short, about 20 minutes back to the pier at the end of the day.

Each island has a different character, which is why three works better than two. Koh Madsum (Pig Island) is the famous one: a white-sand beach where a family of pigs wanders between the trees and the shallows, busy with shared boats from mid-morning. Koh Tan is the snorkelling stop, with a shallow coral reef close to the beach that suits beginners and children. Koh Rap, south-west of Koh Tan, is the quiet one: a long white beach with shade, calm water, a small bar selling drinks and basic toilets, and far calmer than Pig Island at midday.

The captain plans the order around tide and wind, and you can tell him to stay longer, cut a stop short or skip an island altogether. Compared with the two-island private longtail (5,950 THB), you pay 2,500 THB more for the extra island. For a longer, slower day built around Koh Rap, see the Koh Rap full-day private boat.

Who this tour is for

  • Families and groups of up to 8 who want more than the standard two-island trip.
  • Couples looking for a quiet beach away from the shared tours.
  • Visitors who have done Pig Island before and want something new nearby.
  • Anyone who likes a slow, traditional boat and a flexible day.

Who should choose another tour

  • Only want the pigs and a snorkel: the private longtail or the shared speedboat tour.
  • More than 8 guests, or want a faster ride: the private speedboat (up to 10) can add Koh Rap when sea and time allow.
  • Want lunch included and a set itinerary: the small-group longtail tour.
  • Want a full day with long beach time: the Koh Rap full day.

What to bring

  • Cash in small notes for the island fees (about 50 THB per person on Koh Madsum and on Koh Rap) and for lunch and drinks.
  • Snacks and plenty of water on the boat: island bars are basic. Outside drinks can't be taken onto Koh Rap.
  • Reef-safe sunscreen, hats, sunglasses and a long-sleeved layer: shade on a longtail is limited.
  • Swimwear, towels and a change of clothes.
  • A dry bag for phones, and water shoes for rocky shallows.

Good to know

  • Sea by month: January to September is best; February to April is calmest. Morning seas are usually calmer, and the light is better for snorkelling. October to December brings frequent rain and some windy days. The trip runs whenever the sea is safe, and the captain may change the order or drop the furthest island if the wind picks up. If we cancel for weather, you choose a full refund or a new date.
  • Spray and sun: longtails splash in chop, and there is little shade on board.
  • Children: adult and child life jackets are on board and children wear them at all times on the boat. With very young children, keep the day short and skip an island if they tire.
  • Mobility: longtails land on beaches, so expect to step into knee-deep water at each stop.
  • Snorkelling: Koh Tan is the main reef. Don't stand on coral or feed fish.
  • The pigs: watch and photograph them, let them come to you, and don't chase, lift or feed them junk food.
  • Drones: registered drones only (CAAT and NBTC); ask before flying near other visitors or the animals.

Pickup and meeting point

The longtail leaves from Thong Krut pier, and we send the exact location and meeting time on WhatsApp. Hotel transfers can be arranged on request from the main areas of Koh Samui (Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam, Choeng Mon, Bang Rak and Plai Laem). Thong Krut is about 45–60 minutes by road from Chaweng and 30–40 minutes from Lamai. Morning (around 08:00) and afternoon (around 13:00) starts both work; tell us your preference when you book.
